$comment: Machine-readable compliance contract for every payment gateway this
starter can integrate. scripts/payment-compliance-check.mjs reads this
file and audits YOUR project against it: webhook wiring, signature
verification, refund policy surface, terms/privacy reachability and
gateway-specific obligations. It is documentation-as-code: when a
provider changes its contract, this file changes with the docs and the

requirements: refund policy text must state a concrete window
terms and privacy pages must return HTTP 200 on the production URL
webhook endpoint must verify signatures BEFORE any business logic
one-time vs recurring plans must be distinct products at the gateway
support contact e-mail on the site must be a monitored mailbox
common.policyReview: Before first launch and after any gateway change: FETCH each selected gateway's policySources live (web fetch tool or operator pastes the current text), diff against the obligations recorded here, and let the live text win - update this contract in the same PR. Never recite platform terms from memory.

waffo.webhookSignature: RSA-SHA256 over `${t}.${rawBody}` (header t=<ms>,v1=<base64>), verified with the platform public key per environment
ignoreEvents: subscription.payment_succeeded (pure receipt; provisioning on it double-grants)
obligations: Merchant of Record: Waffo is the seller of record - invoices and refunds flow through them
AUP: no prohibited categories (hosted face-swap entry points, adult, gambling...); digital template downloads are allowed
successUrl must point back to your app
buyer identity: checkout email is the license identity

policySources.label: Waffo developer docs (products, checkout, webhooks, AUP notes)
Pancake merchant dashboard - the store policies YOUR account agreed to

stripe.webhookSignature: Stripe-Signature t,v1 HMAC with the webhook signing secret; verify on the raw body
obligations: use a restricted API key, never the secret root key, in production
recurring prices must be real recurring Price objects
billing portal must be reachable for self-serve cancellation

policySources.label: Stripe docs (review, issuing and compliance requirements)

creem.webhookSignature: CREEM-API-SIGNATURE HMAC sha256 over raw body with the webhook secret
obligations: MoR seller of record is Creem
product type one_time vs subscription must match the plan semantics

paypal.webhookSignature: PAYPAL-AUTH-CERT + transmission HMAC verification via verify-webhook-signature API on the raw body
obligations: no billing portal today (documented gap) - cancellation route must exist in-app
user approval at capture time is mandatory for subscriptions

lemonsqueezy.webhookSignature: X-Signature HMAC sha256 with the webhook secret over the raw body
obligations: custom data echo location on webhooks must be re-verified against your account (documented uncertainty)
store checkout links must carry variant + license grant semantics consistently

dataProtection.note: Engineering support for regional data-protection law. Distinguish YOUR BUILD (what the generated project contains) from YOUR TODO (capabilities pruned as operator-side: implement them yourself). This is not legal advice; lawful basis, registrations and processor agreements stay the operator's responsibility.

engineering: in your build: CookieConsent component + no ad trackers; /terms and /privacy pages exist as placeholders - REPLACE the copy before launch
your todo: access/export/erasure endpoints (the starter prunes its reference /api/privacy/* as operator-side - implement equivalents or document who answers requests)
your todo: retention schedule - prune includes no /api/cron/retention; wire one with a CRON secret, 90-day default is a reasonable start
your todo: consent + breach evidence trail (append-only events table or your processor's audit log; keep the support mailbox monitored for the 72h path)
in your build: docs/dpa-template.md ships with this package - fill it out per processor (gateway, hosting, mail) before B2B selling
cross-border: name each processor (Supabase, your gateway, your mail provider) on the privacy page - never hard-code, resolve copy through env config
same controls as GDPR; state the UK in the data map when serving UK buyers
Do Not Sell/Share: honored by construction - the starter ships no ad or tracking scripts; keep it that way
notice at collection: your /privacy placeholder must list every entity and mailbox you actually use
your todo: 45-day access/deletion handling - same DSR surface as GDPR above
GDPR-shaped controls carry it; add a pt-BR privacy page when targeting BR traffic
consent + purpose notice + DPO contact on /privacy
verifiable-consent expectations for minors' data: video/AI features must not target minors
